part.text:
4 tests failed — the naive "always pad with spaces" approach is wrong. Looking at the failing output, the rule is more subtle: trailing spaces are only preserved if they come from actual characters in the input, and padding spaces at the end of the output row (originating from input rows that don't reach that column) must be truncated. For example, in the "many lines" test, the final expected row is `'          ,'` — the last 3 input rows don't reach column 52, so they are completely excluded from that output row. However, in `'  reldi ffd   '`, all 14 rows have actual characters in that column, so the trailing spaces are preserved.

The correct rule: each output row includes input rows from row 0 through the last input row that actually has a character in that column.
